name: FAB FOUR SOLO
clue: Though credited to the Beatles, this 1965 ballad features only Paul McCartney and a string quartet

name: RUN FOR THE AGES
clue: This barefoot Ethiopian palace guard won the 1960 Olympic marathon on Rome's cobblestones, then won again in Tokyo wearing shoes.

name: LONG LIVE THE KING
clue: Becoming king at age four, this French monarch reigned 72 years, outliving both his son and his grandson

name: PLANETARY NAMES
clue: Alone among the eight planets, this one takes its name from Greek rather than Roman mythology

name: COLD WAR CHESS
clue: In Reykjavik in 1972, this American ended a 24-year Soviet grip on the world chess championship

name: BACK FROM THE DEAD
clue: Revived from liturgical use into an everyday spoken tongue, this ancient language became official in the new state of Israel in 1948.

name: JAILHOUSE INK
clue: Begun in a Bedford jail, this John Bunyan allegory follows a burdened man named Christian toward the Celestial City.

name: BROADWAY RECORDS
clue: Running from 1988 to 2023, this Andrew Lloyd Webber musical logged Broadway's longest run at 13,981 performances

name: OLYMPIC CITIES
clue: With the Games of 1908, 1948 and 2012, it became the first city to host the Summer Olympics three times

name: ORGAN RECITAL
clue: This human organ can regrow to full size from as little as a quarter of its original mass

name: BELOW SEA LEVEL
clue: The shores of this hypersaline lake, bordered by Israel and Jordan, are the lowest dry land on Earth

name: NOBEL LITERATURE
clue: In 1913 this Bengali poet of 'Gitanjali' became the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature

name: EPIC TITLES
clue: Homer's epic of the Trojan War takes its title not from its hero but from this alternate name for Troy

name: AND THE OSCAR GOES TO...
clue: This 1969 tale of two New York hustlers is the only X-rated film ever to win the Best Picture Oscar

name: UNFINISHED BUSINESS
clue: This Austrian composer's Symphony No. 8, left with only two completed movements, is known simply as the 'Unfinished'

name: DYSTOPIAN TITLES
clue: Ray Bradbury titled this novel after the temperature at which he was told book paper catches fire

name: ALL THAT GLITTERS
clue: Real gold leaf shimmers in this Austrian painter's portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer and in his famous embracing couple, 'The Kiss'.

name: SHAKESPEARE'S ROMANS
clue: Banished by the city he had saved, this general marches an enemy army to Rome's gates in the Shakespeare tragedy named for him

name: LIGHT THE WAY
clue: Celebrating Rama's return to Ayodhya, this five-day autumn 'festival of lights' fills India with oil lamps and fireworks.

name: UNITS OF MEASURE
clue: The SI unit of magnetic flux density honors this inventor, born in 1856 in what is now Croatia

name: FIRST EMPERORS
clue: After unifying China in 221 B.C., he standardized script, coins, and axle widths; thousands of terracotta soldiers guard his tomb.

name: OVER BEFORE LUNCH
clue: History's shortest recorded war, in 1896, lasted under 40 minutes and pitted Britain against this island sultanate off East Africa.

name: WHAT'S IN A PLACE NAME
clue: Stilt houses on Lake Maracaibo reminded European explorers of a certain canal city, earning this country its diminutive name.

name: CANAL KNOWLEDGE
clue: Nero personally broke ground for a canal across this Greek isthmus in 67 A.D.; the cut wasn't completed until 1893.

name: PERFECT SEASONS
clue: The 1972 edition of this NFL team went 17-0, the league's only unbeaten season capped by a Super Bowl win

name: DOUBLE LAUREATES
clue: This American chemist is the only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes: Chemistry in 1954 and Peace in 1962

name: MAIL BONDING
clue: Told entirely in letters, diaries, and news clippings, this 1897 Gothic novel tracks a count's sea voyage aboard the Demeter.

name: MIDDLE OF NOWHERE
clue: Nicknamed for a Jules Verne captain, this oceanic 'pole of inaccessibility' is where space agencies aim their retiring spacecraft.

name: STELLAR NEIGHBORS
clue: This red dwarf, with a name meaning 'nearest,' is the closest star to our sun

name: THE CONSTITUTION
clue: It's the only constitutional amendment ratified specifically to repeal an earlier amendment
